tasks.short: Advocate with a client in crisis until the immediate problem is addressed.

steps.what: Note the clients and the crises she will advocate.
Fetch the service directory line for that agency.
Check that directory line is the agency she named.
Advocate with patients until the crises ease.
Record the outcome after she does resolve crises.

tasks.design: She notes the clients, the crises and the agency she will call. A fetch from the service directory ({OTHER}) returns only that agency's published line, and she checks it is the same agency. She advocates with the patients and writes the outcome herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The agency number lived in her head or on a paper list, and the crisis could not wait for a search of the whole file.
tasks.enabler_now: A directory can return one published line for an agency she has already named.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to advocate in the room. A missing line does not find the agency for her.
tasks.human_edge: She judges how hard to push, and what the client can bear, while the crisis is happening.
tasks.altitude: The crisis conversation is unchanged. She still decides how to advocate, and she gains a published phone line only when she has named the agency.

reach.task: Keep the local list of service agencies
reach.learn: Which published lines belong in the directory, and which she still finds by phone.

evidence.claim: A lookup of one published phone line does not advocate in the crisis and does not choose the agency. Model knowledge.
A record of a person's health is special-category data under the GDPR rule on special categories.

assumptions: s1 produces the client name, the crisis in her words, and the agency name. s2 reads only the agency name and returns one published phone line, or blank.
She finds a blank line herself. The fetch does not send a referral, raise an alert, or store audio.
unknowns: Which directory holds the published agency lines, and who is allowed to update them.
Whether the outcome note later enters the treatment dossier.
research_questions: How often is the agency she needs already in the directory under the name she uses?

already_counted.description: Reading the directory line against the agency she named is the check in s3.

incremental.description: Check that each stored agency line is still the published number.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a week of crises where she has already named the agency, only the directory lookup is shorter. The advocacy and the outcome note stay. If the agency is absent, the line is blank and she finds the number herself.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain end-of-life symptoms and options so the client can decide.

steps.what: Note the symptoms and the options she will educate on.
Fill one sheet line per option she named.
Check each line quotes an option she named.
Educate clients on those symptoms and those options.
Hear the informed decisions the clients then make.

tasks.design: She names the symptoms and the options she will explain. The {SPREADSHEET} fills one line per named option from stored leaflet text, and she checks it adds nothing. She educates the clients and hears their decisions herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The option leaflets were a pile, so she hunted for the page while the client was waiting.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored leaflet text can be copied onto a sheet for options she has already chosen.
tasks.still_hard: She still explains the symptoms in this client's situation. The sheet does not recommend a path.
tasks.human_edge: She paces the explanation and hears a decision the client is ready to make.
tasks.altitude: The explanation and the client's decision stay hers. The sheet only holds leaflet lines for options she already chose.

reach.task: Explain end-of-life options in plain language
reach.learn: Which stored leaflet lines match the options she has already chosen to explain.

evidence.claim: Copying stored leaflet text for an option she named is not the education and is not a treatment recommendation. Model knowledge.
Symptom names in a client note are special-category health data under the GDPR rule on special categories.

assumptions: s1 produces the symptom labels and the option names she will explain. s2 copies stored leaflet text for those names only, or leaves the line blank.
She explains a blank option from the leaflet herself. The sheet is not filed, is not sent, and does not recommend an option.
unknowns: Which leaflet texts are approved for this service, and in which languages.
Whether the client wants a family member in the room for the explanation.
research_questions: How often does she already know the option names before she sits down with the client?

already_counted.description: Reading each sheet line against the option she named is the check in s3.

incremental.description: Retire a leaflet line when the stored option text changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a week where she has already chosen the options, only the sheet fill is shorter. The explanation and the client's decision stay. A changed leaflet leaves the line blank and she reads it herself.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet other professionals to evaluate the condition and the client's needs.

steps.what: List the patients and the condition facts to assess.
Fill a brief sheet from those condition facts.
Check the brief adds no condition she did not list.
Collaborate with professionals to evaluate that condition.
State the client needs that evaluation supports.

tasks.design: She lists the patients and the condition facts. The {SPREADSHEET} fills a brief from only those facts, and she checks it adds no condition. She evaluates the condition with the other professionals and states the client needs herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The condition facts sat in several notes, and the meeting started before they were in one place.
tasks.enabler_now: A sheet can place only the facts she has already listed.
tasks.still_hard: The evaluation with the other professionals does not get shorter. The sheet does not diagnose.
tasks.human_edge: She weighs a medical fact against what the client needs, with the people who treat them.
tasks.altitude: The meeting and the assessment stay hers. The brief only repeats condition facts she listed.

reach.task: Turn a clinical evaluation into a rehabilitation need
reach.learn: How a stated need is checked against the condition the team just evaluated.

evidence.claim: Copying condition facts she listed does not evaluate the patient and does not assess the need. Model knowledge.
Facts about a patient's condition are special-category health data under the GDPR rule on special categories.

assumptions: s1 produces the patient name and the condition facts in her words. s2 copies those facts into the brief and adds no diagnosis. A missing fact stays blank.
The brief is not sent and is not filed. No alert is raised from a fact on the brief.
unknowns: Which professionals must be in the room before she states a need.
Whether the ward already keeps a structured condition list she can reuse.
research_questions: How often are the condition facts written down before the meeting starts?

already_counted.description: Reading the brief against the condition facts she listed is the check in s3.

incremental.description: Fix the brief when a copied condition fact lands on the wrong line.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a week where she has already listed the condition facts, only the brief fill is shorter. The meeting and the statement of needs stay. A fact she did not list is not added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and coordinate care, then follow through to see if it worked.

steps.what: Plan the care from consultation data and experience.
Draft plan lines that quote that consultation data.

loop.input: The services, dates, efficacy signs and consultation facts she noted in s1.
loop.output: Plan lines that quote only those facts and name the service and the date.
loop.check: Each line quotes a service, a date or a fact she noted. A line that adds a service, a date, a diagnosis or a risk statement she did not note, including suicide, violence or abuse, fails.
loop.stop: One pass. A failing line is dropped. If every line fails, the draft stays blank and she writes the plan.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy cannot say what care was planned, or tell a risk line from a service she named.

steps.what: Check every plan line quotes her consultation data.
Confirm this plan before it is filed.
File the confirmed plan in the case record.
Fill a follow-up sheet from the services she named.
Follow through with the client to judge service efficacy.

tasks.design: She plans the care from the consultation data she notes. A draft in {DOCS} writes plan lines that quote only those facts, she confirms the plan, and a separate write files only that confirmed plan in the case record ({OTHER}). The {SPREADSHEET} fills a follow-up sheet from the services and dates she named, and she judges efficacy with the client.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was typed after the consultation, often from memory, and the follow-up list was a second document.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can quote a note she already wrote, and a sheet can list services she already chose.
tasks.still_hard: She still plans the care and still visits to see whether it worked. A line she did not note is dropped, not repaired.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the care from the consultation and from what she knows of this client, and she judges whether the service worked.

ambition.what: She confirms the written plan before she leaves the ward, on cases where the services and the dates are already in her note.

tasks.altitude: She still plans the care and still judges whether it worked. She confirms the plan text before anything is filed.

reach.task: Set the rehabilitation steps that follow a care plan
reach.learn: Which follow-up dates she should watch herself, and which the sheet may only list.

evidence.claim: Rapportage-assistent drafts a Wmo or Jeugdwet intake report and a worker checks every output.
A Dutch municipal pilot of kitchen-table summaries saved little time because the workers kept their own notes, and it was weaker when several problems were in play.
A published review found invented suicidal ideation in social-work notes produced with transcription tools.
The Amersfoort intake draft was put through a data-protection assessment before use.
A care plan holds special-category health data under the GDPR rule on special categories.
An eligibility decision must not rest on automated processing alone.
Deciding eligibility for public assistance and healthcare services, by or for a public authority, is listed as high-risk. This draft does not decide eligibility.
The Amersfoort register describes the intake draft as a narrow procedural task, and states that profiling stays high-risk.
Where the plan is part of a treatment dossier, Dutch medical-treatment rules keep that dossier for twenty years.
Recording a staff conversation needs works-council consent under the Dutch works-councils act.
The follow-through visit and the choice of services are not produced by the draft. The range uses neither the council hours figure nor the vendor time claim. Model knowledge.

assumptions: s1 produces the service names, the dates, the efficacy signs and the consultation facts she chooses. s2 quotes only those. A risk line she did not write is dropped. If the draft is blank she writes the plan.
s5 files only the version she confirmed in s4. s6 copies the service and the date only. No referral is sent, no efficacy score is produced, and no audio is stored.
unknowns: Whether this care plan sits in the treatment dossier that the medical-treatment rules cover.
Whether this team also writes a municipal support report, which this design does not draft.
research_questions: How often are the services and the dates already in her note before she leaves the room?

already_counted.description: Reading each plan line against her consultation note is the check in s3.

incremental.description: Keep the rule that drops a risk line she did not note, and the blank-draft fallback.

approvals.approved_version: confirmed plan text she accepted in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the services, the dates and the facts are already in her note, the draft, the file and the follow-up sheet replace typing. The planning conversation and the efficacy visit do not shrink. On a week of several problems, where she keeps her own note, only the file and the sheet remain. The council hours figure and the vendor time claim are not used.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the crisis, the education, the ward meeting and the follow-through. Only the agency line, the option sheet, the condition brief, the plan draft, the plan file and the follow-up sheet move.
reach: From a community health worker, which local agency lines are safe to store in the directory.
skills_to_grow: Spot a plan line that adds a risk or a service she did not note.
Keep the service directory to published lines only.
role.ambitious_version: When she has named the services and the dates, she confirms the plan before she leaves the ward. The crisis, the education and the efficacy visit stay hers.
